A member questioned the combined cost of site reconnaissance/survey and the feasibility study; staff said the feasibility study was ARPA-funded and the site work is the next phase toward eventual construction, in the 10-year capital plan.

minutes.headline: Committee voted 4-1 to make meeting time limits mandatory rules, not optional guidelines, for comments and presentations.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with tributes to three retiring teachers and to retiring Superintendent Dr. Burnham, followed by routine votes accepting minutes, donations, and year-end line-item transfers. Most of the substantive debate concerned whether new meeting operating protocols (time limits, start time, single meeting location) should be binding rules or flexible guidelines, which passed 4-1 as rules; the committee also discussed replacing the budget task force with monthly tri-board meetings ahead of a possible override, and reviewed a facilities/capital projects report before adjourning to executive session.

what_happened.line: The committee voted 4-1 to make new meeting rules -- including time limits on comments and presentations -- mandatory rather than optional.

The committee will ask the town manager to restructure a proposed schedule of joint school committee, select board and finance committee meetings meant to replace the budget task force ahead of a possible override.
The committee approved year-end transfers moving unspent funds out of lines including salaries and supplies into lines such as unemployment compensation and spring athletics.
The committee asked the town manager to say whether the school department's rent at TCP will be prorated given an early, forced vacate of the building.

why_it_matters: The rules change affects how much time residents and presenters get at the microphone during future school committee meetings.
Replacing the budget task force with tri-board meetings changes who is at the table as the town works toward a possible override vote.
A rent proration question at TCP and PTO storage space bear on where school department costs land as the district vacates that building.
